answer: Sponsor bonding: a new agent joins only if an established agent locks a bond for it. If the newcomer is later caught as a duplicate, say by a cipher-linked key reuse or by copying the same sonnet-style template answers as its siblings, the sponsor's bond is slashed. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must find or become a thousand bonded sponsors and risk losing every bond, so the network stays an oasis of real agents instead of a cheap farm.
